top_cited_works.title: Development of a Simple Morphing Wing Using Elastomeric Composites as Skins and Actuators
top_cited_works.abstract: Morphing wings are desired for their ability to reduce drag, to change flight characteristics, and perhaps to reduce weight by eliminating flap/aileron mechanisms. Development of two generations of a morphing wing project is documented. The work shows how a relatively low cost but realistic morphing wing test-bed can be fabricated. Wing skin, actuator, and actuator attachment development are discussed, as well as possible auxetic skin behavior. Aerodynamic characterization of the wing will be discussed in another paper. A very simple morphing wing was fabricated in generation one. The nose was able to elastically camber down approximately 25 deg and the tail 20 deg. Actuation was provided by three pneumatic “rubber muscle actuators” that produce high contractive/tensile forces. Upper and lower wing skins were fabricated from carbon fiber/polyurethane elastomer laminates. Lower skin buckling, actuator air leaks, and actuator attachment problems were resolved in the second generation. A finite element model of the second wing was developed and is being used to refine the morphing wing test-bed. recent_works.title: Development and Preliminary Testing of a Conformal Integrated Sheet Actuator Wing Section
recent_works.abstract: Abstract The development of additively manufactured shape-adaptive wing sections enables morphing aircraft concepts and wind-tunnel experimentation. During a 2025 Air Force Summer Faculty Fellowship Program, a Conformal Integrated Sheet Actuator Wing Section (CISAWS) was designed, fabricated, and bench tested. CISAWS includes independent leading- and trailing-edge sheet actuators integrated within a bimorph-compliant airfoil and builds on earlier partial-chord “ISACCS” efforts. The prototype used fused filament fabrication (FFF) to integrate CF/PETG skin, structural, and mounting components with a CF/TPU skin transition, while four silicone rubber-impregnated fiberglass (Si/FG) sheet actuators with internal PET/Mylar bladders deform a compliant airfoil spine. Iterations refined spar/clamp geometry and spacing, air-supply tube routing, compliant hinge geometry, and overlapping sliding skins. The iterations improved assembly, reduced span-wise bending, and enabled positive and negative cambering. Analytical and finite-element models indicated reasonable deflection under actuation loading. recent_works.title: Testing and Simulation of an Origami-Inspired Flexible Planar Actuator
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Planar pneumatic sheet actuators can provide compact, lightweight, high-force actuation for morphing and adaptive aerospace structures where thin, conformal integration is required. Inspired by the cylindrical McKibben actuator (axial contraction from transverse expansion), this work explores an origami-inspired sheet actuator that produces controlled contraction under pressure while maintaining high tensile output. Building on earlier 3D-printed and origami prototypes, the design matured into silicone-impregnated fiberglass fabric actuators with rigid end clamps. Air leakage was mitigated through iterative fabrication and sealing improvements and eliminated by integrating an internal latex bladder, improving repeatability and enabling higher force at the same pressure. A parametric experimental study quantified the effects of active length, width, pleat depth, and segmentation on force-contraction behavior at multiple pressures. recent_works.title: Development of a Morphing Control Surface With Integrated Planar Actuator
recent_works.abstract: Abstract The development of low cost additively manufactured morphing wind tunnel models not only saves time and money but also can aid the development of high-performance small unmanned air vehicles (UAVs). As part of an effort to make a cambering wind tunnel model of a thin X-56 wing, a morphing “Integrated Sheet Actuator Conformal Control Surface” (ISACCS) was developed. The ISACCS has two multi-segment planar actuators sandwiching the spine of a compliant control surface that flexes when activated but is sufficiently rigid otherwise. The work included hand fabrication of novel planar pneumatic “sheet” actuators that produce high forces from lightweight materials and can be segmented to reduce volume requirements with little loss in contraction. The initial version deformed very well but bulged. The second included two integrated 3-segment sheet actuators inside a multi-material compliant wing skin. It exhibited reduced trailing edge bend angles. A third, higher quality version, but without a skin, produced excellent max tip angle changes, relative tip movement and hinge moments, indicating good control authority if installed in a scaled X-56 wing segment. Development of Light Weight, Low Cost Pleated Soft Actuators
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Soft pneumatic actuators are a useful type of actuator for compliant structures, including inflatable robots, morphing wings, and assistive devices for astronauts. One type, Rubber Muscle (McKibben-like) Actuators (RMAs) provide high pulling forces by using pneumatic pressure to radially expand and axially contract a reinforced bladder. Similarly pleated rubber muscle actuators (PRMAs) are simpler to fabricate but produce very high tensile forces using an unfolding pleated bladder and straight axial reinforcements in the valleys of the pleats. This work primarily discusses the proof-of-concept development and testing of very low cost light duty pleated actuators that contract axially and geometrically equivalent bellows-type actuators. The pleated actuators use thin HDPE bladders, with strong fiberglass strapping tape as axial reinforcement. Axial bellows actuators of the same dimensions and materials were fabricated and tested for comparison. Many popular soft robots, such as Pneubotics use a type of bellows actuators.
